tagline: The old Sauk Trail, from the Lake Michigan shore to Detroit.
intro: From New Buffalo, where the state highway department opened the nation's first highway travel information center in 1935, US-12 runs east across the bottom of Michigan through Niles, Mottville, Sturgis and Coldwater, into the lake country of the Irish Hills and on through Ypsilanti and Dearborn to Woodward Avenue in downtown Detroit, 208 miles.

The line is a Native American trail that settlers called the Sauk Trail. In 1820 Henry Schoolcraft found it a plain horse path that a stranger could not follow without a guide for all its side trails. In 1825 the federal government surveyed it into the Chicago Road.

moments.title: Mottville Bridge
moments.text: The fourth bridge at the old Sauk Trail ford of the St. Joseph, a 1922 concrete camelback now kept for walkers. A farmer bought its covered predecessor and built a barn from it.

moments.title: Coldwater
moments.text: A town of five historic districts and the Tibbits Opera House, the second-oldest theatre in Michigan, with the Capri Drive-In just west on the highway.

moments.title: Irish Hills
moments.text: Hills and kettle lakes named for the Irish who settled them in the 1830s and 1840s. Of the old roadside attractions, the dinosaur forest and Fantasy Land have closed, and Mystery Hill carries on.

sources.label: MDOT, Pure Michigan Byways Driving Guide (Wayback Machine snapshot, December 2025)
